va_new_leaves.label: Haute Couture & Fashion Design
va_new_leaves.defn: Dress designed by a named couturier or fashion house and shown in collections — haute couture (the Chambre Syndicale's protected label, from Worth in 1858) and designer ready-to-wear — placed by designer; the garments and collections are the works (Dior's New Look, 1947; Chanel's suit; Balenciaga's sack dress). Regional and folk dress stays in its own H7 leaf; tailoring traditions (Savile Row, Neapolitan) are H7-14 and H7-15.
va_new_leaves.aliases: couture; haute couture; fashion design; designer fashion
va_new_leaves.see: H7-14 Savile Row Tailoring; J1-5 Fashion Photography; N Design.
catalogues: every runway show of the fashion houses, by season and designer
dress from the 17th century to today
va_new_leaves.axis: designers by country of their house, in the order France, Italy, United Kingdom, United States, Japan, other countries; rows in date order
